domain_entities.name: AccrualPeriod
attributes: start: Date (UTC day start, inclusive boundary)
end: Date (UTC day start of the following period, exclusive boundary)
domain_entities.purpose: Derived value object representing the half-open accrual period [start, end) that contains a given date. Computed on demand by periodContaining, anchored on an employee's hireDate and stepped by a policy's accrualPeriodMonths. It is never persisted — it is derived from Employee.hireDate and LeavePolicy.accrualPeriodMonths and used to key LeaveBalance rows.

business_rules: Accrual date arithmetic reads UTC fields only (getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate) and derives day boundaries at UTC midnight; it must never use local-time getters. node-pg parses DATE columns to local midnight while this arithmetic reads UTC fields, so any local-time read silently shifts every accrual period by a day on a non-UTC server. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever accrual period derivation (startOfUtcDay) appears, not only here]

An accrual period is a half-open interval [start, end): a date belongs to the period when start <= date < end (inclusive start, exclusive end). The end boundary is the start of the next period, not the last day of the current period. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever accrual period containment (periodContaining) appears, not only here]

addMonths advances the month and clamps the day-of-month to the last day of the target month (e.g. Jan 31 + 1 month → Feb 28/29; Mar 31 + 1 → Apr 30). It never rolls over into the following month. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever month arithmetic (addMonths) appears, not only here]

periodContaining anchors on the hireDate's UTC day start and steps accrualPeriodMonths periods at a time; it throws ConflictError('Requested date precedes the accrual anchor') when date < anchor and ConflictError('Unable to resolve accrual period') when no period resolves within the 10,000-iteration safety bound. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever accrual period derivation (periodContaining) appears, not only here]

startOfUtcDay, addMonths, and periodContaining each have exactly one canonical definition (src/shared/date/accrual.ts); every consumer imports them from the shared entry point (src/shared/date) rather than maintaining a private copy, so the arithmetic cannot drift between call sites. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever accrual date helpers appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
This feature is a pure refactor (deduplication) with no new entities, lifecycle states, or state transitions. The domain concept at stake is the AccrualPeriod value object and the three pure UTC date helpers (startOfUtcDay, addMonths, periodContaining) that derive it. These helpers are foundational arithmetic shared by the leave and balance modules; their semantics are BINDING and must hold identically at every call site.

Key domain facts recorded:
- AccrualPeriod is a derived, non-persisted value object { start, end } representing the half-open interval [start, end) containing a date, anchored on Employee.hireDate and stepped by LeavePolicy.accrualPeriodMonths. It keys LeaveBalance rows via findByKey.
- The helpers read UTC fields only (getUTC*) and derive day boundaries at UTC midnight. This is load-bearing: node-pg parses DATE columns to local midnight while the arithmetic reads UTC, so any local-time read shifts accrual periods by a day on non-UTC servers. This is a broad business rule, not a narrow implementation detail.
- Period containment is half-open (start <= date < end); addMonths clamps day-of-month to the target month's last day; periodContaining throws ConflictError for date-before-anchor and loop-exhaustion (10,000-iteration bound).
- The deduplication itself is a broad rule: exactly one canonical definition of each helper exists, and all consumers import from src/shared/date.

No lifecycle states are introduced or changed by this feature (the existing Employee/LeaveBalance/LeavePolicy/LeaveRequest lifecycles are untouched). No open questions: the arithmetic is already settled and the feature is a pure move with behaviour preserved.
